podcasts.name: No Priors
podcasts.title: Taking on ServiceNow: Coding Agents the Rest of Us with Serval Co-Founder and CEO Jake Stauch
podcasts.description: What happens when you put code-generation agents in the hands of enterprise IT teams? With Serval, you get a system where it's easy for everyone to be a builder. Sarah Guo and Elad Gil sit down with Serval co-founder and CEO Jake Stauch to analyze his company’s direct challenge to ServiceNow as the enterprise automation and service management system of record. Jake explains that by building an AI platform for enterprise IT departments with Serval, users can safely build while still safeguarding permissions by strict deterministic approvals and an audit trail. He also talks about ProServal, the company’s team that embeds automation engineers directly with customers in order to provide ongoing support and service. Jake also discusses how AI was the big unlock to taking on ServiceNow, why he’s betting on coding agents getting even better, why consumer is a window into what will happen next in enterprise and why the SaaS-pocalypse might look more like a consolidation, why background agents are still a moonshot in enterprise software, and the importance of hiring product-oriented engineers. Sign up for new podcasts every week. podcasts.name: Unsupervised Learning
podcasts.title: Ep 95: Modal CEO on the Future of Inference, the Chaos of the GPU Market & Origins of the Sandbox Bet
podcasts.description: Jacob Effron and Pat Chase sit down with Erik Bernhardsson, co-founder and CEO of Modal, for his second appearance on Unsupervised Learning, now with the company past a $1B run rate. They dig into how the AI compute market actually works behind the scenes, why Modal’s early bets on sandboxes and low-level infrastructure paid off, and Erik’s takes on NeoClouds, NeoLabs, and where GPU prices are headed next.   (0:00) Intro (1:26) The Compute Market Today (5:16) Modal’s Path to LLM Inference (10:02) Building the Hard Infrastructure (12:32) Unsolved Problems in Inference (16:07) Chips & Model Sizes (21:21) What Wins in Inference (24:56) Prioritizing a Multi-Product Roadmap (30:20) Agents as Modal’s Users (33:19) The Next Big Bet After Sandboxes (38:58) Robotics & Multimodal Inference (41:04) Scaling From $2M to $1B (42:51) NeoClouds & NeoLabs (48:15) RL as a Service (51:40) Quickfire   Pat is an AI investor at Redpoint Ventures. He’s led Redpoint’s investments in companies like Modal, Serval & Hex. Follow Pat on Twitter: https://x.com/patrickachase Jacob is an AI investor at Redpoint Ventures. He's led Redpoint's investments in companies like Abridge, Physical Intelligence & Legora. Follow Jacob on Twitter (@jacobeffron). On Unsupervised Learning we probe the sharpest minds in AI in search for the truth about what's real today, what will be real in the future and what it all means for businesses and the world. If you're a builder, researcher or investor navigating the AI world, this podcast will help you deconstruct and understand the most important breakthroughs and see a clearer picture of reality. Subscribe to this show to stay up to date on our latest episodes.

podcasts.name: AI & I by Every
podcasts.title: Can You Use AI To Make Good Art? — With Fred Graver
podcasts.description: Subscribe to Every (free for 14 days): https://every.to/youtube-every-offer Can AI create good art?  Fred Graver thinks the answer depends on you. The Emmy Award–winning writer, producer, and founder of AI Writer’s Studio says AI can help with many parts of the creative process—but it can’t give you something to say. Without your own point of view, AI will only make your work more average. On this week’s episode of The Every Podcast, Natalia Quintero sits down with Graver. They discuss why every writer should have a ‘who I am as a writer’ document, the cast of AI collaborators he’s built into his own writers’ room, and the human quirks that make characters endearing—the part he insists AI can’t supply.
